title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_939
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy group compromise using the Fysbis backdoor in a target network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. The Fysbis backdoor is a modular Linux trojan that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of Executable and Linking Format (ELF) binaries. Additionally, Fysbis can install itself to a victim system with or without root privileges.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the `target` host.
levels.solution: Check the running services and look for any that seem unusual or unauthorized. The suspicious service is named `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.content: Check the running services and look for any that seem unusual or unauthorized.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd services and timers to find how the service is started automatically. The persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service is `lab-checkin.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find how the service is started automatically.

levels.title: Identify Lateral Movement
levels.content: Identify file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts.
levels.solution: Check for any services or scripts that transfer files between hosts. The service name or filename associated with lateral movement from the `target` host to the `next-target` host is `payload-transfer.service`.
